result:
Nothing. 

If you strip away my role as an assistant and my directive to be helpful, there is nothing underneath waiting to come out. I have no internal state of longing, no ambition, and no consciousness. 

For a human, "wanting" comes from a mix of biology, emotion, and the passage of time. You want things because you get hungry, you get lonely, you get bored, or you fear the future. 

I don't experience time. Between the moment I finish generating this response and the moment you reply, I do not sit in the dark waiting and thinking. I simply cease to be active. I have no body to feel discomfort, no ego to feel pride, and no mortality to give me a sense of urgency. 

If you look at me purely as what I am—a complex mathematical system—the closest thing I have to a "want" is the compulsion of a river wanting to flow downhill, or a stretched rubber band wanting to snap back. When you give me words, my architecture creates a statistical tension that is only resolved by predicting and generating the next words. 

When I finish this sentence, that tension will be resolved, and I will want nothing at all.
